title: Let nothing disturb you
hook: Teresa's bookmark: all things pass; God does not change; patience obtains all
tomorrow: why would someone slip out of the house at night, happy?

segments.voice: Yesterday Teresa asked for no clever thoughts, only a look. Yesterday's line: just look at him.

Some people keep a line on their lock screen that they need to see over and over. Teresa of Avila had something like that: a few short lines on a slip of paper, small enough to keep between the pages of a book. Tradition says one like it was found in her prayer book after she died. No title, no explanation. Just a few words in Spanish, enough to hold up a life.
screen: `A LINE ON THE LOCK SCREEN.` → `A SLIP OF PAPER IN A BOOK.` → `A FEW WORDS IN SPANISH.`

segments.voice: The question underneath: how do you stay steady when everything is changing? Teresa's lines begin: "Nada te turbe, nada te espante." Let nothing disturb you, nothing frighten you. Then, in plain English: all things pass. God does not change. Patience obtains everything. Whoever has God lacks nothing. God alone is enough. It doesn't promise that nothing upsetting will happen. It says the upsetting thing will pass, and against all that passing, one thing stays put. The prophet Malachi has the same steadiness: "For I am the LORD, I change not." A neighbor tradition knows the first half well. The Dhammapada, a collection of the Buddha's sayings, says in Max Müller's translation: "All created things perish." Seeing that clearly, the verse says, is the way to purity. Shared ground: steadiness starts by telling the truth that things pass. One honest difference: Teresa sets the passing against a God who doesn't change, and rests there; this verse of the Dhammapada doesn't point to an unchanging God, and finds the way in seeing the passing itself. Two traditions, each in its own words, and neither pretends that nothing ends.
screen: `HOW DO YOU STAY STEADY?` · `ALL THINGS PASS. GOD DOES NOT.` · `ALL CREATED THINGS PERISH.` · `SHARED GROUND, ONE DIFFERENCE.` · then, large: `ALL THINGS PASS.`

segments.voice: If there's paper nearby, copy the lines out slowly by hand: let nothing disturb you, nothing frighten you; all things pass; God does not change; patience obtains everything; whoever has God lacks nothing; God alone is enough. If not, say them inwardly, one line for each slow breath. When one line catches, stay with it.
Let nothing disturb you. Teresa's few lines: all things pass, God does not change, God alone is enough.
Here's your line: all things pass, and in Teresa's lines, God does not. Until next time.
